title: feat: list MCP servers and pricing alongside models
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds an MCPs tab to the official model catalog
- Lists registry-backed descriptions, environment-specific endpoints, and Pollen rates
- Reuses model billing-adjustment metadata and pricing rows for MCP tools
- Exposes the same billing details from `GET /mcp`
- Keeps MCPs separate from model API responses and model sorting

gist.headline: The toolbox gets a shelf
gist.blurb: The model catalog now has a proper corner for MCP servers. Their endpoints, descriptions, and Pollen rates have stopped hiding in the shed.
gist.summary: Added an MCP Servers tab to the official catalog and a GET /mcp endpoint that expose registry descriptions, environment-specific endpoints, Pollen rates, and shared billing-adjustment details without mixing MCPs into model responses or sorting.
gist.impact: Developers can now browse available MCP tools and their exact connection and pricing details in the catalog or via GET /mcp before putting them to work.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the model catalog as a cozy garden library with a newly opened MCP toolbox shelf: labeled tool cards show a plug icon, endpoint paths, and tiny Pollen price badges. Polli, wearing a tiny librarian visor, is filing MCP cards beside a retro CRT robot that happily displays an organized catalog; code-plants and flowers make the technical directory feel alive.
gist.image_prompt: A cozy pixel art garden-library scene where a cute CRT monitor robot proudly opens a new catalog tab labeled “MCP SERVERS,” showing chunky tool cards with tiny endpoint lines and Pollen price badges, while code-plants sprout from flower pots around the shelf. The main character is a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings; she wears a tiny librarian visor and files a card into the new shelf. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft lime green (#ecf874) and pastel gradient background, chunky retro sprites, warm lighting, lo-fi vibes like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike, subtle CRT glow, nostalgic but beautiful.
